heroHeadline: China Rejects US 'Distillation' Accusations as HBM Shortage Drives 20-50% AI Chip Price Hikes; Tencent-Backed Enflame Triples in Shanghai Debut
heroSubtitle: September 11, 2026 — Three developments this week trace the strain and momentum inside China's domestic AI buildout. On September 9, China's Foreign Ministry and Commerce Ministry both rejected the September 8 US joint advisory accusing six Chinese AI firms of industrial-scale distillation of American frontier models, with spokesperson Mao Ning calling the claims 'unfounded accusations and smears' rooted in China's 'technological self-reliance,' and MOFCOM countering that distillation is a 'common practice' US labs use too — neither ministry disputed the advisory's specific technical claims. On September 10, Reuters reported that Huawei, Cambricon, MetaX, and Iluvatar CoreX have all raised AI accelerator prices 20-50% as a high-bandwidth-memory shortage, driven by 2024 US export controls, pushes Chinese chipmakers toward costly grey-market memory; Huawei's Ascend 950DT now tops 250,000 yuan (~$37,255), up from levels quoted just two months earlier. On September 11, Tencent-backed Enflame Technology closed its Shanghai STAR Market debut up 179% versus its IPO price (intraday peak +234%), valuing the chipmaker at roughly $25.5 billion — more than triple its IPO valuation — making it the fourth of China's 'AI Chip Four Little Dragons' to go public in 2026. Together the week shows China's domestic chip ecosystem simultaneously absorbing a real supply-side memory cost shock and continuing to attract outsized capital-market enthusiasm, while Beijing holds a firm diplomatic line against US distillation allegations weeks before Xi Jinping's planned September 24 Washington visit.
